From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>

Thanks for the flag, Tom — that's exactly the symptom I mentioned. Looks like the forwarded .ics stripped the VTIMEZONE block and left a floating DTSTART. That's what causes the different clients to interpret the wall-clock hour relative to the recipient's default zone instead of the intended zone.

Root cause (quick): the first .ics (demo-invite.ics) was author-generated and didn't include a full VTIMEZONE. When I created the Google invite I generated a standard Google .ics (redwood-invite.ics) but when Kate forwarded her original .ics to Tom the client merged/forwarded the original attachment instead of the Google event. Tom's import therefore saw the floating DTSTART.

Action taken: I just created and sent a corrected invite that explicitly contains a VTIMEZONE for America/Los_Angeles and Europe/London and also updated the event directly on the Google event so it should appear correctly in all calendars. Attachment: redwood-invite-fixed.ics.

Please confirm reception and the displayed local time for you, Tom (SGT). I'll also paste a direct meeting link here if anyone wants to add it manually: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=redwood-demo-ACME-20260721

Apologies for the friction — we will join Tue Jul 21, 15:00 BST / 07:00 PDT / 22:00 SGT.

Thanks,
Lauren
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
